transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in today because... I just can’t stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. It's really bothering me. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just don't see it. I feel like it’s the very first thing the families I work with, the nurses, or even people at church notice when they look at me. I just can't seem to get past it.
Because of how you feel about your jaw and neck, do you find yourself repeatedly checking mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?

Yes, I do. Um, especially right before I leave for work or a meeting. I just keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I'll stand there fixing my collar, or pulling my hair around my neck to try and hide it. Then I usually take another look using my phone camera just to see how it looks from another angle. Sometimes I even ask my daughter if it looks strange to her. It's... well, it's actually made me late more than once because I just get stuck doing it.

Aside from the concerns about your jaw and neck, do you experience any other repetitive, unwanted thoughts or routines you feel compelled to perform, such as excessive cleaning, counting, or checking things?

No, not really. I mean, I like to keep a clean house and all, but I don't feel like I *have* to do it over and over. I don't count things or check the stove a bunch of times or anything like that. It's really just... just the thing with my neck and jaw that I get stuck on.
Deep down, do you ever think that your perception of your neck and jaw might be slightly exaggerated or not quite as bad as you see it, or are you completely convinced that it is truly defective?

I mean, I know other people say it looks fine, and... sometimes I wonder if maybe I'm making it a bigger deal than it is. But when I look in the mirror, it's all I can see. It just looks so obvious and terrible to me. So, even if part of me thinks maybe it's not as bad as I feel it is, I just can't shake the feeling that it's really noticeable and ugly.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in physical appearance (jaw and neck sagging/unevenness) that is not observable or considered normal by others. This preoccupation is accompanied by repetitive behaviors including frequent mirror checking, camouflaging with hair and clothing, taking photos, and seeking reassurance, resulting in functional impairment (lateness). Symptoms are specific to appearance concerns without generalized obsessions or compulsions, consistent with ICD-10 Body Dysmorphic Disorder (classified under F45.2 Hypochondriacal disorder).
